newsitem.title: UK: Gold OTC option vols very low, expiry seen dull.
newsitem.headline: Gold OTC option vols very low, expiry seen dull.

text.p: Volatilities in gold OTC options bumped along at historically low levels and the expiry on Tuesday was expected to have little effect on the underlying price, dealers said.
"Volatility at one-month 4.0 percent bid is as low as you can go, really. There hasn't been much of a change from a week ago," a dealer said.
Gold at-the-money one-month implied volatilities were bid at 4.0 percent, three-month at 4.3 to 4.75 percent, six-month at 5.5 percent and one year at 6.2 to 6.5 percent.
At the start of October one-month volatilities were around half a percentage point higher.
Open interest on October options expiring on Tuesday was seen on every dollar in the recent underlying range of $380-$385, which has contained gold for much of the past two months, dealers said.
"In gold there's nothing too spectacular in the pipeline, there are no heavy strikes within reach," a dealer said.
But one dealer noted that the $383 level had a heavier concentration of open interest.
"People were expecting it be staying at this $383 level, which is unusual, but I think we'll see it here tomorrow," the dealer said. "Then it's $380 if it fails at the $382 level."
Business was quite thin as people waited for the underlying price to break out the $380-$385 band
"Basically sentiment is that people want to see it break out. As long as it stays confined to a very small range they would rather not do anything at all," one dealer said.
"Volumes have been pretty low. We haven't seen any particular buying of low delta or up cycles," he added.
In silver, the key strike price remained $5.00 calls, although dealers said they did not expect it to be in the money on Tuesday.
"If anything it is more likely it will get caught in between areas. I wouldn't expect too much from silver," a dealer said.
